title: My Days at the Pension Board
content: Before the firm, I was an economist at Michigan's state pension board in Lansing. My job was briefing the trustees - teachers, retired cops, a couple of political appointees - on what the research said about the fund. [laughter] Nothing quite like a room full of people responsible for hundreds of thousands of retirements asking you hard questions about your spreadsheet. It was incredible training. But here's what I learned: a pension fund is like steering an ocean liner. You can nudge the direction, but slowly, and the effects don't show up for years. I wanted to help people more directly. That's what drew me to the firm.
follow_up: In Lansing I saw how one decision in a boardroom rippled down to real families - a retired schoolteacher's check, a cop's survivor benefit. It gave me a deep respect for how connected everything is. That perspective still shapes how I think about investing and life planning.
